title: Three tables
prompt: Show each customer's name, order id as order_id, and the quantity of each item. Replace the ___ with the second join.
starterSql:
SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id, i.quantity
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
___;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id, i.quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id, i.quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i;
wrongSolutions.why: The second join has no condition

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, o.id AS order_id, o.id AS quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;

title: Four tables
prompt: Show each customer's name and the name of each product they bought, as product.
hints: Walk from customers to products through two tables.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, p.name AS product FROM customers c JOIN products p ON p.id = c.id;
SELECT c.name, i.product_id AS product FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id;
wrongSolutions.why: Shows an id, not a name

title: Report rows
prompt: Show each student's name, the course title, and the grade, for every enrolment.
hints: enrolments connects the other two tables.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.grade FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.grade FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.student_id;
wrongSolutions.why: Uses the wrong column for courses

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, e.course_id, e.grade FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id;

title: Best-selling by customer
prompt: Show each customer's name and their total units bought, as units, sorted by units descending, then name.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY units DESC, c.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS units FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY units DESC, c.name;
SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY units, c.name;

title: Keep everyone through two joins
prompt: Show every customer's name and their total units bought, as units, with 0 for customers who bought nothing.
hints: Both joins must be LEFT JOINs.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity), 0) AS units FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity), 0) AS units FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
wrongSolutions.why: The inner join loses unmatched customers

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(i.quantity) AS units FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

title: Fix the chain
prompt: This should show each order's id and product name as product, but one join links to the wrong column, giving wrong rows. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT o.id, p.name AS product
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;

title: Revenue from good customers
prompt: Show the name of customers with total shipped revenue above 50, using price times quantity, and that total as revenue.
hints: Filter status in WHERE, and revenue in HAVING.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE order_items SET quantity = 2 WHERE order_id = 11 AND product_id = 7;

solutions: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'shipped' GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING SUM(p.price * i.quantity) > 50;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING SUM(p.price * i.quantity) > 50;

SELECT c.name, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE o.status = 'shipped' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

title: Subject averages per year group
prompt: Show each year_group and subject, with the average grade rounded to 1 decimal as average, sorted by year_group then subject. Use only enrolled students.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.year_group, c.subject, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.year_group, c.subject ORDER BY s.year_group, c.subject;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.year_group, c.subject, ROUND(AVG(e.grade), 1) AS average FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.year_group ORDER BY s.year_group, c.subject;

SELECT s.year_group, c.subject, AVG(e.grade) AS average FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.year_group, c.subject ORDER BY s.year_group, c.subject;
